factions.name: Xevos
factions.description: Military biotech empire that crushed the old Imperium; pursuing advanced tech and genetic material across the sector.
goals: Acquire bio-samples from Salvax Prime
Eliminate Ghost Armour threats
Expand influence via proxies rather than direct confrontation
Complete development of the Contagion
Hunt down remaining Imperium (Rax) remnants

recentActions.action: Sent Orrax + Shift to retrieve a cache from Salvax Prime

nextActions.trigger: If the crew escaped with the cache
If the crew destroyed the cache

arc.title: Quiet Proxy Expansion
arc.groundTruth: Xevos avoids direct confrontation, building the Contagion secretly, expanding influence through deniable proxies (including funding the Ashfall Remnant).

rumors.text: A Xevos bio-research vessel has gone dark near the Kess Reach — some say it's testing something they call the Contagion out where no one's supposed to be watching.
Xevos bounty postings for "Rax-marked" individuals have tripled this month.
rumors.note: GM-only: postings are genuinely up, but bounty-hunter guilds are exaggerating the multiplier to justify demanding higher rates.

rumors.text: A supply convoy bound for a Xevos proxy garrison was intercepted and stripped clean — officially blamed on raiders, but the precision reads more like sabotage.

arc.advanceCondition: The Contagion program reaches a visible testing/resourcing milestone — natural trigger point is Reptoids reaching Stage 3.

arc.title: Contagion Nears Completion
arc.groundTruth: Testing intensifies, resource demands spike, draws harder on Dark Star output.

rumors.text: Word from a scared engineer: the Contagion isn't built for the battlefield. It's built for atmospheres — whole colonies, breathed in before anyone knows to run.

arc.title: The Squeeze Tightens
arc.groundTruth: Fear of last-minute sabotage drives Xevos to hunt Imperium harder and crack down on Ghost Armours.
arc.crossFactionTrigger: Makes Imperium eligible to advance to Stage 3, and Zurin eligible to advance to Stage 2.

arc.title: Resolution
arc.groundTruth: Branches: Contagion deployed (a real, dark escalation) OR stopped at the last moment.

local.name: Ress Talvane
local.description: Sells manifest data for coin, terrified of being caught.

distant.name: Director Vael Ostrum
distant.role: Xevos bioweapons researcher, rumored Contagion architect
distant.description: A name spoken with dread, not casually met.

factions.name: Zurin
factions.description: An ideological movement, open to any species, led by the prophet Reph. Actively organizing against Xevos.
goals: Oppose Xevos expansion
Recruit allies
Gather intelligence on Xevos technology

nextActions.action: Send an emissary to recruit the party

arc.title: Growing Openly
arc.groundTruth: Reph preaches openly, recruits, gathers intelligence on Xevos technology.

rumors.text: Reph gave a sermon on an open channel last week — unencrypted, unafraid. Either she's certain of her cause, or she's daring Xevos to finally silence her.
A Zurin cell on the outer rim reportedly turned three Xevos-aligned scientists to their cause.
There's a rumor the Zurin have started training their own pilots, not just preachers.
rumors.note: GM-only: a handful of self-defense volunteers, wildly overstated by the rumor into an implied military buildup.

arc.advanceCondition: Xevos reaches Stage 2-3 and starts treating Zurin's open defiance as a direct target rather than background noise.

arc.title: Direct Provocation
arc.groundTruth: Xevos moves against Zurin directly. Forces a choice: go underground, or escalate.

arc.title: Alliance or Break
arc.groundTruth: Branches: real anti-Xevos coalition with Reptoid resistance and/or Imperium remnants, OR internal fracture under pressure.

local.name: Brother Dessen
local.description: Trades info/aid for genuine kindness toward the movement.
local.agenda: GM-only: sincere, but frames every piece of news in the most Zurin-favorable light without realizing he's doing it.

factions.name: Ghost Armours
factions.description: Consciousness-transfer victims seeking vengeance on the Rax — the ruling caste of the old Imperium — and liberation from a form of immortal torture. Typically act alone or in small fighting units rather than as a unified faction; every Ghost Armour, without exception, wants the Imperium hunted down.
goals: Hunt remaining Rax/Imperium survivors
Destroy consciousness-transfer technology
Free other Ghosts still bound to armor

arc.title: Isolated Hunters
arc.groundTruth: Individuals and small units hunt independently, no coordination, no shared intelligence network yet beyond rumor of one.

rumors.text: A lone Ghost Armour tore through a Xevos listening post looking for Imperium records — left the Xevos crew alive. Word is Ghosts only kill Rax, not their captors.
rumors.note: GM-only: true in this instance, but the generalization is shakier than the rumor implies — a few Ghosts have killed collaborators too. Popular belief runs ahead of fact here.

rumors.text: A Ghost calling itself "the Patient One" has been spotted watching an Imperium-linked auction house for weeks without moving. Whatever it's waiting for hasn't happened yet.

arc.advanceCondition: Imperium reaches Stage 2 — more visible Imperium activity means more independent Ghosts stumbling onto the same leads.

arc.title: Crossed Paths
arc.groundTruth: Independent Ghosts start finding the same leads without coordinating — old grudges even among the vengeful.

arc.title: The Choir Speaks
arc.groundTruth: Enough near-simultaneous success pushes the first real coordination — "the Choir of the Bound" becomes more than rumor.

local.name: Vess
local.description: Mostly given up the hunt; trades old knowledge for help with a personal loose end.

distant.name: The Choir of the Bound
distant.description: Contacting them means finding just one Ghost and earning trust to be introduced further.
distant.agenda: GM-only: individual Ghosts share real intel but each carries their own grudges and blind spots — no single Ghost has the full picture, so any one contact's info is incomplete even when sincere.

factions.name: Imperium
factions.description: The old ruling order, crushed but not extinguished — Rax remnants and loyalists operating covertly, squeezed between Xevos (who hunts them for sport and resources) and the Ghost Armours (who hunt them for vengeance).
goals: Undermine Xevos from within
Preserve/recover lost Imperium technology and knowledge
Avoid detection by Xevos and Ghost Armours alike
Rebuild influence through proxies and old debts

arc.title: Scattered Survival
arc.groundTruth: Remnants hiding, small-scale sabotage, quietly buying back old Imperium-era tech through cutouts. Actively running counter-intelligence, including planting false leads about survivor locations.

rumors.text: A Xevos administrator was found dead in his own sealed office last week — no forced entry, no leads. Some say it has the mark of the old Imperium's methods.
Rumor holds a Rax bloodline survives in hiding on a backwater world, protected by locals who owe an old debt no one talks about.
rumors.note: GM-only: this is an Imperium-planted decoy rumor, meant to draw Xevos hunters toward the wrong world while the real survivors stay hidden elsewhere. Whoever repeats it may not know they're spreading disinformation.

rumors.text: Imperium loyalists are said to be buying up derelict Imperium-era tech at absurd prices, no questions asked, through a dozen cutout buyers.

arc.advanceCondition: Xevos reaches Stage 2 (the Contagion becomes an existential threat worth open risk to stop).

arc.title: Coordinated Sabotage
arc.groundTruth: Recognizing the Contagion as existential, remnants coordinate more openly.

arc.title: Exposure Risk
arc.groundTruth: Increased visibility draws Xevos's intensified hunt and easier Ghost Armour tracking. Forces a real choice: go fully underground, or risk open action.
arc.crossFactionTrigger: Makes Ghost Armours eligible to advance to Stage 2.

local.name: Kellis Vane
local.description: Claims no loyalty to the old order but clearly still does favors for someone in it.
local.agenda: GM-only: genuinely works for Imperium remnants and will feed convincing disinformation (like the decoy-world rumor) to anyone he doesn't fully trust — including the party, at first.

distant.name: The Unnamed Rax
distant.description: Known only by an encrypted comm-sigil left at sabotage sites.
distant.agenda: GM-only: not actually contactable as a reliable source — anyone claiming direct contact with them is probably lying or mistaken.

factions.name: Reptoids
factions.description: A species in open civil war over a captured Dark Star being used to fuel new Xevos-adjacent superweapons. Splintered between loyalists still fueling the Dark Star program, an emerging resistance trying to stop them, and factions now in direct skirmishes with Xevos itself.
goals: Resistance: destroy or nullify the Dark Star program
Loyalists: complete the Dark Star weapon before it's stopped
Both: avoid becoming fully absorbed as Xevos proxies

arc.title: Brewing Civil War
arc.groundTruth: Loyalists fuel the captured Dark Star in secret for a new superweapon program; a resistance is organizing to stop them, but open fighting hasn't started yet.

rumors.text: A Reptoid loyalist convoy was ambushed by its own kind near a fueling relay — resistance forces, hitting a Dark Star supply line in broad daylight. The civil war isn't hiding anymore.
A resistance cell is reportedly offering real coin for anyone who can get them close to a Dark Star containment site — recruiting outsiders now, not just their own kind.
Word going around a cantina circuit claims the Dark Star has already gone unstable and is going to detonate any day now.
rumors.note: GM-only: baseless panic-rumor, probably started by someone trying to spike black-market prices on evacuation gear.

arc.advanceCondition: Resistance successfully sabotages a major supply line (openly, undeniably) OR loyalists complete a visible show of force.

arc.title: Open Conflict
arc.groundTruth: Sabotage/retaliation becomes undeniable, sector-wide news. Civil war is now common knowledge.

arc.title: Xevos Intervenes
arc.groundTruth: Xevos moves to seize the faltering Dark Star program directly rather than let it collapse. First open Reptoid-Xevos clashes.
arc.crossFactionTrigger: Makes Xevos eligible to advance to Stage 2 (Contagion nears completion).

arc.title: Resolution
arc.groundTruth: Branches: Dark Star destroyed/contained (Xevos loses its fuel source) OR seized by Xevos (Contagion surges forward).

distant.name: Marshal Thessrix
distant.description: Oversees a Dark Star containment site. A name spoken with real fear.

factions.name: Kitt
factions.description: A newly-expanding species pushing to establish a genuine multi-planetary presence for the first time, leveraging their renowned quickness as pilots and gunfighters to stake claims faster than rivals can contest them.
goals: Establish colonies/claims on additional worlds
Build alliances that legitimize their expansion
Avoid provoking a faction with the power to crush the effort early

arc.title: Early Expansion
arc.groundTruth: Claim-staking, generous trade delegations, colony ships — genuinely independent of the main conflict so far, but their expansion path is drifting near contested Reptoid space, and Kitt claims are starting to encroach on Kessel Salvage Guild's traditional territory.

rumors.text: The Kitt planted a formal claim-flag on a moon nobody else wanted — until they showed interest. Now three other outfits are suddenly interested too.
A Kitt trade delegation is touring independent stations, offering startlingly generous terms — buying goodwill fast, before anyone bigger notices the expansion.
A Kitt colony ship went missing en route to a new claim — no distress call, no wreckage found yet. Bad omen for the whole expansion push.
rumors.note: GM-only: not bad luck — the ship strayed near a Dark Star-adjacent conflict zone and got caught in Reptoid-on-Reptoid crossfire. Nobody's connected the dots publicly yet.

arc.advanceCondition: Normal expansion friction escalates into real rivals contesting claims.

arc.title: Contested Claims
arc.groundTruth: Real rivals push back — ordinary expansion friction, not yet the main war.

arc.title: Caught in the Crossfire
arc.groundTruth: The Reptoid/Xevos conflict spills into or near a Kitt claim, forcing a real political choice.

local.name: Fennik
local.description: Young, eager, terrible at hiding what he's actually doing.

distant.name: Matriarch Korrivane
distant.description: A name that carries real weight in any Kitt settlement.

factions.name: Free Traders
factions.description: Independent merchant network; Maye operates the local node from Outpost Kess.
goals: Maintain trade routes
Broker between factions
Maximize profit

recentActions.action: Maye contacted the party with the Salvax Prime cache opportunity

nextActions.action: Maye pays the party's share, offers the next contract

factions.name: Meridian Corporate Authority
factions.description: The most outwardly respectable of the four. Bankrolls legitimate colonies, disaster relief, infrastructure — genuinely does enormous public good, which makes the rest easier to hide.
factions.specialty: Finance, underwriting, insurance — the "bank" face of the conspiracy
goals: Out-underwrite the other three guilds until every major contract in the sector runs through Meridian credit.

Collective (shared, GM-only): Behind the competition, an unofficial council of guild heads works patiently to make every government and faction financially dependent on guild credit, guild shipping, and guild contract law — until political sovereignty is hollow and guild economic power is the only authority that actually functions. Not conquest. Erosion.
factions.darkTruth: Functions as the de facto bank for organized crime across multiple factions — loan-sharking and money laundering on a sector-wide scale, dressed as ordinary finance.

local.name: Underwriter Corvassa Lyne
local.description: Smooth, genuinely helpful on the surface, terrifyingly good at not-quite-lying. A plausible first thread to pull — she knows more than her rank should allow.
local.agenda: GM-only: loyal to the guild above all else; will feed just enough true information to seem trustworthy while protecting anything that actually matters.

factions.name: Obsidian Concordat
factions.description: The sector's largest legitimate weapons supplier, openly proud of it — 'we arm those who keep the peace.'
goals: Become the sole approved arms supplier for every major power, public and private.

Collective (shared, GM-only): Behind the competition, an unofficial council of guild heads works patiently to make every government and faction financially dependent on guild credit, guild shipping, and guild contract law — until political sovereignty is hollow and guild economic power is the only authority that actually functions. Not conquest. Erosion.
factions.darkTruth: Quietly arms multiple sides of the same conflicts simultaneously — including both Reptoid loyalists and the resistance — and its 'security consultants' are functionally an assassination-for-hire operation.

local.name: Quartermaster Bregga Sol
local.description: Blunt, transactional, treats every conversation like a weapons sale — which, in a sense, it always is.
local.agenda: GM-only: sincerely believes arming everyone equally is 'keeping balance,' not funding a war — a true believer in the guild's own cover story.

factions.name: The Ferrous Compact
factions.description: Controls more cargo lanes than any single government fleet. 'If it moves, it moves through us' is practically their slogan.
goals: Own enough chokepoint routes that no rival guild can move goods without Compact tariffs.

Collective (shared, GM-only): Behind the competition, an unofficial council of guild heads works patiently to make every government and faction financially dependent on guild credit, guild shipping, and guild contract law — until political sovereignty is hollow and guild economic power is the only authority that actually functions. Not conquest. Erosion.
factions.darkTruth: Runs the sector's largest smuggling network through its own legitimate shipping lanes, and periodically stages 'pirate' attacks on rivals' cargo — blamed on real pirates, executed by their own people.

local.name: Dockmaster Ilyan Vosk
local.description: Overworked, underpaid, and just cynical enough to let things slip he shouldn't — if you catch him on a bad day.
local.agenda: GM-only: genuinely resentful of the guild, one of the few contacts who might actually want to talk if approached carefully.

factions.name: The Covenant Exchange
factions.description: The guild that 'writes the rules' — every major trade contract in the sector uses Covenant Exchange standard terms, enforced by their own arbitrators.
goals: Make Covenant contract law the de facto legal system, superseding local/planetary courts entirely.

Collective (shared, GM-only): Behind the competition, an unofficial council of guild heads works patiently to make every government and faction financially dependent on guild credit, guild shipping, and guild contract law — until political sovereignty is hollow and guild economic power is the only authority that actually functions. Not conquest. Erosion.
factions.darkTruth: Holds enormous quantities of blackmail material through 'confidential' contract terms, and enforces predatory debt clauses that amount to legalized indentured servitude — all technically within the letter of agreements people signed without reading closely enough.

local.name: Arbitrator Thess Calloway
local.description: Polite, precise, and utterly without visible remorse — everything they do is 'technically' within the contract.
local.agenda: GM-only: not lying, exactly — genuinely believes contract law is a fair, neutral system, and can't or won't see the predation baked into it.
